epoch_ai.synthesis: Epoch estimates the cost of hitting a fixed benchmark score has fallen about 13x per year over five years, which it says is 4x faster than DNA sequencing and 6x faster than compute cost (Sept 28, summary of a longer report). Sept 24: Huawei will make roughly 25x less total compute than Nvidia in 2026 and, Epoch expects, stay around four years behind through 2030. Read via direct fetch (the cron's Epoch pull is 403-blocked).

semianalysis.synthesis: Sept 28: analysis of how sparse attention in GLM5.3 changes memory demand (HBM and NAND); Sept 25: launched a China datacenter model. Written from the feed summaries only; the articles were not read.

farmdoc_daily.synthesis: Sept 25: Iowa farmland (Iowa State survey, since 1941) and Mato Grosso land compounded at 7.7% and 8.7% a year over 2002-2025; Mato Grosso peaked at $11,145/acre in 2022 and fell to $9,066 in 2025 while Iowa held roughly flat since 2024, leaving Iowa 27% higher. The authors tie Brazil's drop to lower profits, cost pressure and tight credit.

drought_monitor.synthesis: Indiana as of Sept 22: 3.2% abnormally dry (D0), 0.0% moderate drought (D1), against 3.8% D0 on Sept 8. Last week's note recorded 8.7% D0 for Sept 15; that reading is not in the history ledger (the pre-fix dedupe dropped it), so the fall is against that figure only.

nass_crop_progress.synthesis: Week ending Sept 27, Indiana corn: 95% dented, 62% mature (12% on Sept 6), 13% harvested for grain; soybeans 74% dropping leaves, 14% harvested.

interconnection_fyi.synthesis: Indiana holds 56 tracked data-center projects (33 proposed, 13 cancelled, 6 under construction, 4 operational), unchanged in every daily snapshot since Sept 12. That is expected for a slow-moving series; the national benchmark below shows where it sits.

noaa_ncei_monthly.synthesis: August 2026 was very wet in Indiana: 7.2 in. station-average precipitation, consistent with Purdue Extension's record-rainfall report, with temperatures near seasonal (73.0°F avg; highs 82.7°F, lows 63.3°F). Michigan: 68.0°F, 2.9 in. That wet month is the backdrop for the drought monitor's three-week rise in abnormally-dry coverage since.

equitable_growth.synthesis: Sept 24: a debt-to-wealth lens on government debt across the US, France, Japan and the UK. The authors argue a low ratio of debt to top-0.1%-wealth means narrow wealth taxes could raise a lot relative to debt, which they say describes the US more than countries with lower wealth inequality.

ipcc.synthesis: Sept 28: nearly 200 authors are in Bangkok (Sept 8 to Oct 1) for the Working Group III second lead-author meeting on AR7 mitigation; a First-Order Draft, open to expert review, follows. Otherwise administrative items.

beige_book.synthesis: Sept 2 Beige Book, Chicago District: activity rose slightly in July and early August; consumer spending and construction and real estate were flat on balance, business spending fell slightly, prices rose moderately, and farm income expectations for 2026 improved some. Nationally, growth was modest: 10 of 12 Districts reported slight to moderate growth and two reported no change. Next edition Oct 14.

indiana_dnr_water.synthesis: Indiana DNR, August: statewide rainfall 200% of normal and all 12 tracked streams above normal. Groundwater: above normal at 4 of 9 wells, near normal at 4, well below normal at 1 (LaGrange 2). Drought Monitor showed isolated abnormally-dry spots (Sept 8), and the seasonal outlook has no drought through at least November.

fia_indiana.synthesis: USFS 2025 evaluation for Indiana: 4.83M acres of forest, 14.07B cu ft growing stock. Annual mortality is 1.18% of standing volume (sampling error 5.5%), essentially level with 1.19% in the 2024 evaluation; net growth is 2.23%. First reading in this series.

mrcc_monthly_summary.synthesis: Midwest average temperature for August 2026 was 71.8°F, 0.9°F above the 1991-2020 normal (MRCC monthly summary). First reading in this series; the September summary is not out yet.

interconnection_fyi_national.synthesis: Across 46 US state pages (3,866 projects) the tracker's largest active pipelines are Virginia (329), Texas (282) and Ohio (86); Indiana is 4th at 39, 4.0% of the 972 nationwide, but 32nd in operating sites (4 of 2,435). The tracker's own headline (12,538 records) does not reconcile with its state pages, so read ranks as rough and watch the trend. First reading in this series.

epoch_datacenters.synthesis: Epoch AI's dataset of large AI data centers (93 sites, 73 drawing power) totals 13.5 GW today, 88% of it in the US and 5% in China. Indiana's three sites, led by Anthropic-Amazon New Carlisle (910 MW), come to 1.09 GW, about 8.1% of that covered total (a covered set, not world capacity). First reading in this series; data updated Sept 28.
